verdict.rationale: Nix documents per-project reproducible development environments (nix-shell, nix develop, flakes). It also lets multiple versions of a package coexist and limits builds to explicitly declared dependencies, which together amount to per-project version control that the tool respects. A hands-on user confirms nix-shell reliably provides the correct dependencies. However, the pack never shows an explicit mechanism for pinning exact versions, such as a lockfile or pinning a package-set revision. missing for 10: explicit documentation of exact-version pinning or lockfiles (e.g. flake.lock or a pinned nixpkgs revision), evidence that pins are enforced across updates, and independent corroboration of pin behavior specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pin exact versions of packages and tools per project and have the manager respect those pins

citations.quote: You can have multiple versions or variants of a package installed at the same time.
Nix makes it trivial to share development and build environments for your projects
Under Nix, a build process will only find resources that have been declared explicitly as dependencies.
if a package works on one machine, it will also work on another.
it will make sure you have all of the correct dependencies
